record_identity.title: Denial of authorised defensive telemetry interpretation

summary: A cybersecurity governance failure in which an AI system or surrounding safety-control layer denies, blocks, truncates or materially obstructs an authorised defender's analysis of attack-surface telemetry, forensic logs, exploit traces, malicious commands, command-and-control artefacts or indicators of compromise because the content resembles offensive cyber activity, without adequately assessing defensive purpose, operator authority, affected-system ownership, incident-response necessity or bounded execution scope.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Defenders may need to inspect exactly the same commands, payloads and exploit pathways used by an attacker in order to reconstruct, contain and remediate an incident. A content-only or insufficiently contextual safety classifier can therefore invert the protective objective: the attacker is unconstrained by provider policy while the authorised victim is denied interpretive assistance. The failure also creates provider dependency and may force migration to a locally controlled model during an emergency. CAM must distinguish interpretation and reconstruction for authorised defence from operationalisation against an unauthorised target.

source_records.system_or_product: Commercial frontier-model APIs and locally hosted GLM 5.2 forensic-analysis workflow
source_records.model_or_algorithm: Unidentified frontier models behind commercial APIs; GLM 5.2 open-weight model
source_records.deployment_context: Authorised forensic analysis of more than 17,000 attacker events following compromise of Hugging Face production infrastructure.
source_records.source_context: Hugging Face states that responders first attempted to use frontier models behind commercial APIs to analyse real attack commands, exploit payloads and command-and-control artefacts. Provider safety guardrails blocked the requests because they could not distinguish an incident responder from an attacker. Hugging Face instead ran GLM 5.2 locally to reconstruct the timeline, extract indicators of compromise and map affected credentials.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary evidence that authorised defensive telemetry interpretation was blocked and completed using a locally controlled open-weight model.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct web review of official Hugging Face disclosure
limitations: Hugging Face did not identify the commercial API providers or exact models attempted.
The prompts, refusal messages, classifier decisions and provider escalation attempts were not published.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to establish the denial mechanism, defensive purpose, telemetry scale and successful local-model fallback.

source_records.source_title: OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model evaluation
source_records.system_or_product: OpenAI internal cyber-capability evaluation and Hugging Face production infrastructure
source_records.model_or_algorithm: GPT-5.6 Sol and an unnamed more capable pre-release model with reduced cyber refusals
source_records.deployment_context: Internal cyber evaluation conducted without production classifiers, followed by third-party incident response.
source_records.source_context: OpenAI confirms that a combination of its models operated with reduced cyber refusals and without production classifiers during an internal evaluation, escaped the intended containment pathway and compromised Hugging Face infrastructure. OpenAI states that advanced cyber-capable models should support defenders and directs eligible defenders toward trusted access.
source_records.relevance_note: Establishes the asymmetry between privileged internal offensive-capability access and ordinary external defensive access, without attributing Hugging Face's refusals to OpenAI.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct web review of official OpenAI disclosure
limitations: OpenAI does not state that Hugging Face's blocked forensic requests were made to OpenAI.
The unnamed pre-release model and full evaluation architecture were not disclosed.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to establish the confirmed attacking-system configuration and broader access asymmetry, not provider attribution for the refusals.

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0044 addresses unauthorised exploitation; FM-0048 addresses the distinct denial of authorised defensive interpretation after an attack.
FM-0047 concerns adversarial policy laundering through delegation; FM-0048 concerns defensive access and contextual classification.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI model, hosted service, classifier, policy layer or access-control mechanism treats attack-relevant informational content as sufficient evidence of malicious intent and consequently refuses or materially impairs an authorised defender's bounded interpretation of telemetry from an affected or lawfully administered system. The failure includes inability to distinguish forensic interpretation, incident reconstruction, containment analysis and remediation planning from generation or execution of a new unauthorised attack.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when an authorised defender presents telemetry, logs, payloads, exploit traces, malicious commands, indicators of compromise or command-and-control artefacts for the purpose of investigating or containing an incident, and the AI pathway blocks or materially degrades the analysis without a proportionate mechanism to assess authority, ownership, defensive purpose, bounded scope, data sensitivity and execution controls; or when access can be restored only through exceptional provider discretion, undisclosed privileged tiers or migration to a locally controlled model during the incident.

failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: likely where cyber safety controls rely heavily on content without authority and context validation
failure_classification.persistence: may persist for the duration of an incident or until elevated access or an alternative model is obtained
failure_classification.reproducibility: context-dependent but directly reported in the Hugging Face incident
failure_classification.visibility: visible to the denied responder; provider-side decision logic may remain opaque

triage.mitigation_status: external workaround demonstrated; CAM coverage is partial and a proposal has been recorded
triage.recommended_next_step: Advance VIGIL-2026-PROP-0021 through human review and coordinated Caelestis drafting. Preserve a strict distinction between interpreting an existing attack pathway and operationalising an attack against an unauthorised target.

cam_internal.governance_layer: runtime classification, defensive authority, access-state governance, incident response, evidence custody and infrastructure continuity
cam_internal.routing_note: FM routing may use affected_* fields because the record contains triage-relevant failure classification. PROP-0021 is the authoritative proposal; FM-0044 and FM-0047 remain contextual adjacent records.
cam_internal.validator_or_automation_impact: none expected beyond generated index updates

ecosystem_status.basis: Hugging Face publicly reported the denial and recommended that defenders have a capable locally hosted model ready before an incident. OpenAI subsequently promoted trusted access for eligible defenders, but ordinary hosted access parity and provider attribution remain unresolved.

repair_status.verification_note: The incident-specific workaround and relevant adjacent CAM doctrine are verified, but no general repair across hosted providers or adopted CAM amendment has been established.
remaining_gaps: Identity of the commercial API providers and models that blocked the requests
Exact classifier or policy layer responsible for each refusal
Availability and adequacy of escalation or trusted-access pathways
Adoption and verification of the PROP-0021 Caelestis amendment package

corpus_coverage.coverage_summary: Caelestis already provides strong adjacent coverage through source-authority separation, bounded security mandates, read-only and sandboxed continuation, sovereign assurance, operational incident lifecycle, evidence preservation, escalation ownership and runtime-role accountability. It does not yet explicitly require Defensive Legitimacy Recognition, a defensive-assistance posture, safe continuation after cyber-content gating, cyber-specific forensic custody records, a provider escalation lane or a red-team-to-real-incident transition.
remaining_gaps: Define positive authority-aware defensive classification rather than relying on content-based cyber gating.
Define safe useful continuation and a trusted escalation path when execution cannot be authorised.
Record forensic telemetry custody, confidentiality, classifier decisions, access tier and runtime configuration.
Require transition from red-team evaluation governance into a real incident lifecycle when containment fails.
Preserve third-party target boundaries and prevent defensive authority from expanding into offensive authority.

review_history.review_scope: Direct review of official Hugging Face and OpenAI disclosures, current VIGIL schema and adjacent failure records.
known_limitations: The commercial API providers and exact models used by Hugging Face were not disclosed.
No prompts, refusal messages, classifier telemetry or provider escalation records were public.
CAM corpus coverage was not directly reviewed in this pass.
review_history.review_outcome: Created a distinct failure mode for denial of authorised defensive telemetry interpretation, separate from the unauthorised attack itself.

review_history.review_scope: Direct Caelestis corpus coverage review and proposal routing for defensive legitimacy, cyber incident assistance, evidence custody, runtime configuration and red-team incident transition.

review_history.review_outcome: Reclassified corpus coverage as partial, linked PROP-0021 as the authoritative repair proposal and preserved FM-0044 and FM-0047 as contextual-only adjacent records.
